fun_facts: Derrick Henry was born in Yulee, Florida. At age 7, he was running past 9-year-olds, and at age 9 he was taking on 11-year-olds.
At Yulee High School, Derrick Henry broke the national career rushing record, finishing with 11,612 yards. In one game, he ran for 482 yards and six touchdowns.
Derrick Henry won the 2015 Heisman Trophy after leading the FBS in carries, rushing yards and rushing touchdowns.
In Alabama’s national championship game, Derrick Henry became the school’s all-time leading rusher; he finished the season with 2,219 rushing yards and 28 touchdowns.
In 2020, Derrick Henry rushed for 2,027 yards, becoming the eighth NFL player to reach 2,000 rushing yards in a season. That total was the fifth-highest in NFL history at the time.

excerpts:
Yulee (Fla.) High School four-star running back [Derrick Henry](https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/108717/derrick-henry) broke the national career-rushing yards record during a 41-26 playoff victory against Perry (Fla.) Taylor County on Friday night.

Derrick Henry of Yulee (Fla.) High School, shown here in a file photo, is the nation's new high school rushing leader with 11,612 career yards.

Alabama](https://www.espn.com/college-football/team/_/id/333/alabama-crimson-tide) commit, surpassed Ken Hall's previous record of 11,232 yards on a 52-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. Hall, who held the record for nearly 60 years, played at Sugar Land (Texas) High School from 1950-53.

Henry finished the night with 482 yards and six touchdowns on 58 carries.

excerpts:
Needing 223 yards in Week 17 to rush into NFL history, [Derrick Henry](https://www.nfl.com/players/derrick-henry/) rumbled into greatness.

Henry ran roughshod over the Houston Texans on Sunday to become the eighth player in NFL history to rush for 2,000 yards in a season.

Henry rushed past 2,000 with a six-yard run in the fourth quarter of Tennessee's [41-38](https://www.nfl.com/games/titans-at-texans-2020-reg-17) win that clinched an AFC South division title. His 250 yards on the day gave him 2,027 for the season, the fifth-most in NFL history.
Henry had the fifth 200-yard outing of his five-year career en route to the Alabama product becoming the third former Heisman Trophy winner to run for 2,000.
